text: On the grey morning when the first turbines began turning in Tessaly Fjord, engineers from Northfold Energy Authority confirmed the tidal plant’s rated capacity at 240 megawatts, enough, they said, to supply roughly 180,000 homes along the northern coast. The facility, a sweep of steel housings and submerged rotors near Kestrel Point, has been years in the making, with early surveys dating back to 2016 and full construction beginning after a 2021 coastal compact. Director Mara Venn called the opening “a measured answer to an old problem,” noting that the fjord’s strong tidal range made it an unusually reliable site. For residents of Saltmere and Bracken quay, the project promises steadier power and a quieter dependence on imported fuel.
